title: The Young Investigator’s Kit
learning_focus: Problem, materials, procedure, findings; units mg/g/kg/°C/mL/L; tools and simple investigation planning.
story_premise: A new investigation kit has no labels or sequence. The player prepares it to answer whether air or water has mass.
mission_objective: Complete the three connected areas and apply the mission learning focus: Problem, materials, procedure, findings; units mg/g/kg/°C/mL/L; tools and simple investigation planning.

areas.title: Problem Desk
areas.story: Choose a testable question. Select balance, containers, thermometer, and measuring tools.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Science Guide
opening_dialogue.text: The station in Problem Desk is not working correctly.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Science Guide
opening_dialogue.text: Observe carefully, investigate Problem, materials, procedure, findings, record the evidence, and use it to restore the station.

learning_clues: Science focus: Problem, materials, procedure, findings.
Record observations and measurements before forming a conclusion.

questions.prompt: Before changing the setup, what should the learner do?

options.text: Observe the starting condition and record a prediction.
Change several things at once.
Choose a conclusion before observing.
Skip directly to the collectible.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Make a prediction from the clues already observed.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: A prediction is recorded before the investigation and is not scored as right or wrong.
questions.correct_feedback: A prediction is recorded before the investigation and is not scored as right or wrong.

questions.prompt: Which record is the strongest scientific evidence?

options.text: A direct observation or measurement from the investigation.
A guess made after seeing the answer.
A detail unrelated to the setup.
A reward animation from the game.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Evidence comes from what was observed or measured.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Scientific evidence is a direct observation or measurement from the investigation.
questions.correct_feedback: Scientific evidence is a direct observation or measurement from the investigation.

questions.prompt: The learner should record the result before choosing a conclusion.

options.text: True
False

questions.first_wrong_hint: A conclusion must be supported by recorded evidence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is true: results are recorded first, then used to form a conclusion.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is true: results are recorded first, then used to form a conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which action best completes this science area?

options.text: perform the guided investigation for Problem, materials, procedure, findings and record what changes or stays the same
Change every variable and do not record the result.
Select an answer without examining the setup.
Send the answer key to the server for scoring.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose the action that connects observation, investigation, and evidence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The learner should perform the guided investigation for Problem, materials, procedure, findings and record what changes or stays the same.
questions.correct_feedback: The learner should perform the guided investigation for Problem, materials, procedure, findings and record what changes or stays the same.

areas.world_action: perform the guided investigation for Problem, materials, procedure, findings and record what changes or stays the same
areas.world_result: The scientific solution restores the station or environment in Problem Desk.
